tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

A UI task records its baseline commit and allowed surface before the first edit. `verify`
refuses changes outside that surface or protected paths, enforces a diff budget and runs
the project's fast proof command, the snapshot inventory proof and the style drift lint.
`allow` records intended inventory removals; `finish` also requires a recorded human
review; `abort` restores only the surface, leaving unrelated work intact.

import json

from dataclasses import dataclass

from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

# messages stay descriptive; consumers match on the code, never on prose.
FINDING_CODES = (
    ("the UI contract changed", "ui.contract-changed"),
    ("the baseline moved", "ui.baseline-moved"),
    ("protected path changed:", "ui.protected-path"),
    ("path outside surface", "ui.outside-surface"),
    ("diff budget:", "ui.budget"),
    ("fast UI proof failed", "ui.fast-proof"),
    ("UI snapshot proof failed", "ui.snapshot-proof"),
    ("UI snapshot proof printed no inventory", "ui.snapshot-empty"),
    ("UI snapshot proof lost", "ui.snapshot-lost"),
    ("style literal", "ui.style-literal"),
    ("human review not recorded", "ui.review-missing"),
)

    """The stable code for one verify/finish finding; unknown prose is `ui.other`."""
    text = str(message)
    for prefix, code in FINDING_CODES:

    return "ui.other"

    """JSON-safe findings with stable codes and the original human message."""

"""
Mechanical UI proofs for the opt-in UI guard (ADR-160).

The snapshot layer turns a project-declared inventory command's output into sorted,
deduplicated lines, so a lost control or handler is a removed line; the style layer
flags hardcoded color and font literals in added surface lines outside the theme
paths the contract declares. Both are pure and deterministic: no I/O, no framework.

PRINCIPLE-003, PRINCIPLE-006, PRINCIPLE-014.
"""

import fnmatch
import os
import re
from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple

MAX_REPORTED_ENTRIES = 8
STYLE_PATTERNS = (
    re.compile(r"#[0-9a-fA-F]{8}\b|#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}\b|#[0-9a-fA-F]{4}\b|#[0-9a-fA-F]{3}\b"),
    re.compile(r"\brgba?\("),
    re.compile(r"\b(font(?:_size|_name|_family)?)\s*="),
    re.compile(r"\bfont(?:-family|-size|-weight)?\s*:"),
)


def matches_pattern(path: str, patterns: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
    """One relative path against contract patterns; `dir/**` covers the tree."""
    candidate = path.replace("\\", "/")
    if os.name == "nt":
        candidate = candidate.casefold()
    for pattern in patterns:
        normalized = pattern.replace("\\", "/")
        if os.name == "nt":
            normalized = normalized.casefold()
        if normalized.endswith("/**"):
            base = normalized[:-3]
            if candidate == base or candidate.startswith(base + "/"):
                return True
        elif fnmatch.fnmatchcase(candidate, normalized):
            return True
    return False


def snapshot_lines(output: str) -> List[str]:
    """Sorted, deduplicated non-empty lines of a UI inventory dump."""
    return sorted({line.strip() for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()})


def inventory_findings(baseline: Sequence[str], current: Sequence[str],
                       allowed: Sequence[str]) -> List[str]:
    """Removed inventory entries are findings unless an allowed pattern matches."""
    present = set(current)
    removed = [line for line in baseline
               if line not in present
               and not any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(line, pattern) for pattern in allowed)]
    if not removed:
        return []
    shown = "; ".join(removed[:MAX_REPORTED_ENTRIES])
    entries = "entry" if len(removed) == 1 else "entries"
    return [f"UI snapshot proof lost {len(removed)} {entries}: {shown}"]


def style_findings(added: Sequence[Tuple[str, int, str]],
                   theme_paths: Sequence[str]) -> List[str]:
    """Hardcoded color and font literals in added surface lines are findings.

    Without declared theme paths the lint is off: nothing is outside a theme.
    """
    if not theme_paths:
        return []
    findings: List[str] = []
    for path, number, text in added:
        if matches_pattern(path, theme_paths):
            continue
        for pattern in STYLE_PATTERNS:
            match = pattern.search(text)
            if match:
                literal = match.group(1) if match.lastindex else match.group(0)
                findings.append(f"style literal '{literal}' outside theme paths: "
                                f"{path}:{number}")

"""
The phase plan: which phase follows which, and how long each one runs.

A session alternates focus and break phases. Every `cycle_length`-th break is a long
one. The plan is a frozen value with no clock and no I/O, so a phase sequence is
reproducible from its index alone.

PRINCIPLE-009, PRINCIPLE-010.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

FOCUS = "focus"
SHORT_BREAK = "short-break"
LONG_BREAK = "long-break"

MIN_SECONDS = 1
MAX_SECONDS = 24 * 60 * 60


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Phase:
    """One phase of a session: its kind and its full duration in seconds."""

    kind: str
    seconds: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PhasePlan:
    """Durations and cycle length for a session's phase sequence."""

    focus_seconds: int = 25 * 60
    short_break_seconds: int = 5 * 60
    long_break_seconds: int = 15 * 60
    cycle_length: int = 4

    def validated(self) -> "PhasePlan":
        """The same plan, or a ValueError naming the field that is out of range."""
        for field in ("focus_seconds", "short_break_seconds", "long_break_seconds"):
            seconds = getattr(self, field)
            if not isinstance(seconds, int) or not MIN_SECONDS <= seconds <= MAX_SECONDS:
                raise ValueError(f"{field} must be an int between {MIN_SECONDS} and {MAX_SECONDS}")
        if not isinstance(self.cycle_length, int) or self.cycle_length < 1:
            raise ValueError("cycle_length must be an int of at least 1")
        return self

    def phase_at(self, index: int) -> Phase:
        """The phase at a zero-based index: even indexes focus, odd ones break."""
        if index < 0:
            raise ValueError("phase index must not be negative")
        if index % 2 == 0:
            return Phase(FOCUS, self.focus_seconds)
        focus_done = index // 2 + 1
        if focus_done % self.cycle_length == 0:
            return Phase(LONG_BREAK, self.long_break_seconds)
        return Phase(SHORT_BREAK, self.short_break_seconds)

"""
Session state and its transitions.

A session is a frozen value: an index into the phase sequence, whether it is running,
when the current run started and how much of the phase was already spent. Every
transition returns a new state, and the clock is always passed in, so the whole model is
deterministic and testable without sleeping.

`settled` carries a state forward across phases that elapsed while nobody was watching,
which is what lets a browser poll a few times a minute without losing phases.

PRINCIPLE-003, PRINCIPLE-009, PRINCIPLE-014.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from typing import Optional

from tempo.phases import FOCUS, PhasePlan

MAX_SETTLE_STEPS = 512


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SessionState:
    """Where a session stands: its phase, its run clock and its finished focus count."""

    phase_index: int = 0
    running: bool = False
    started_at: Optional[float] = None
    spent_seconds: float = 0.0
    completed_focus: int = 0

    @staticmethod
    def initial() -> "SessionState":
        """A fresh, paused session at the first focus phase."""
        return SessionState()


def elapsed_seconds(state: SessionState, now: float) -> float:
    """Seconds spent in the current phase, including the run in progress."""
    spent = state.spent_seconds
    if state.running and state.started_at is not None:
        spent += max(0.0, now - state.started_at)
    return spent


def remaining_seconds(state: SessionState, plan: PhasePlan, now: float) -> float:
    """Seconds left in the current phase, never below zero."""
    phase = plan.phase_at(state.phase_index)
    return max(0.0, phase.seconds - elapsed_seconds(state, now))


def started(state: SessionState, now: float) -> SessionState:
    """The session running from `now`; starting a running session changes nothing."""
    if state.running:
        return state
    return replace(state, running=True, started_at=now)


def paused(state: SessionState, now: float) -> SessionState:
    """The session paused, banking the elapsed run; pausing a paused one is a no-op."""
    if not state.running:
        return state
    return replace(state, running=False, started_at=None,
                   spent_seconds=elapsed_seconds(state, now))


def advanced(state: SessionState, plan: PhasePlan, now: float) -> SessionState:
    """The next phase, from a standing start, counting a finished focus phase."""
    finished_focus = plan.phase_at(state.phase_index).kind == FOCUS
    return SessionState(
        phase_index=state.phase_index + 1,
        running=state.running,
        started_at=now if state.running else None,
        spent_seconds=0.0,
        completed_focus=state.completed_focus + (1 if finished_focus else 0),
    )


def settled(state: SessionState, plan: PhasePlan, now: float) -> SessionState:
    """
    The state with every phase that ran out before `now` advanced past.

    Overshoot carries into the new phase, so a browser that polls late lands on the same
    phase it would have reached by polling every second. The step cap bounds the work a
    single long gap can ask for (PRINCIPLE-010).
    """
    current = state
    for _ in range(MAX_SETTLE_STEPS):
        if not current.running or remaining_seconds(current, plan, now) > 0:
            return current
        overshoot = elapsed_seconds(current, now) - plan.phase_at(current.phase_index).seconds
        current = advanced(current, plan, now)
        current = replace(current, started_at=now - max(0.0, overshoot))
    return current


def reset(state: SessionState) -> SessionState:
    """A fresh session, keeping nothing from the old one."""
    return SessionState.initial()

"""
Session state and its transitions.

A session is a frozen value: an index into the phase sequence, whether it is running,
when the current run started and how much of the phase was already spent. Every
transition returns a new state, and the clock is always passed in, so the whole model is
deterministic and testable without sleeping.

`settled` carries a state forward across phases that elapsed while nobody was watching,
which is what lets a browser poll a few times a minute without losing phases.

PRINCIPLE-003, PRINCIPLE-009, PRINCIPLE-014.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from typing import Optional

from tempo.phases import FOCUS, PhasePlan

MAX_SETTLE_STEPS = 512


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SessionState:
    """Where a session stands: its phase, its run clock and its finished focus count."""

    phase_index: int = 0
    running: bool = False
    started_at: Optional[float] = None
    spent_seconds: float = 0.0
    completed_focus: int = 0

    @staticmethod
    def initial() -> "SessionState":
        """A fresh, paused session at the first focus phase."""
        return SessionState()


def elapsed_seconds(state: SessionState, now: float) -> float:
    """Seconds spent in the current phase, including the run in progress."""
    spent = state.spent_seconds
    if state.running and state.started_at is not None:
        spent += max(0.0, now - state.started_at)
    return spent


def remaining_seconds(state: SessionState, plan: PhasePlan, now: float) -> float:
    """Seconds left in the current phase, never below zero."""
    phase = plan.phase_at(state.phase_index)
    return max(0.0, phase.seconds - elapsed_seconds(state, now))


def started(state: SessionState, now: float) -> SessionState:
    """The session running from `now`; starting a running session changes nothing."""
    if state.running:
        return state
    return replace(state, running=True, started_at=now)


def paused(state: SessionState, now: float) -> SessionState:
    """The session paused, banking the elapsed run; pausing a paused one is a no-op."""
    if not state.running:
        return state
    return replace(state, running=False, started_at=None,
                   spent_seconds=elapsed_seconds(state, now))


def advanced(state: SessionState, plan: PhasePlan, now: float) -> SessionState:
    """The next phase, from a standing start, counting a finished focus phase."""
    finished_focus = plan.phase_at(state.phase_index).kind == FOCUS
    return SessionState(
        phase_index=state.phase_index + 1,
        running=state.running,
        started_at=now if state.running else None,
        spent_seconds=0.0,
        completed_focus=state.completed_focus + (1 if finished_focus else 0),
    )


def settled(state: SessionState, plan: PhasePlan, now: float) -> SessionState:
    """
    The state with every phase that ran out before `now` advanced past.

    Overshoot carries into the new phase, so a browser that polls late lands on the same
    phase it would have reached by polling every second. The step cap bounds the work a
    single long gap can ask for (PRINCIPLE-010).
    """
    current = state
    for _ in range(MAX_SETTLE_STEPS):
        if not current.running or remaining_seconds(current, plan, now) > 0:
            return current
        overshoot = elapsed_seconds(current, now) - plan.phase_at(current.phase_index).seconds
        current = advanced(current, plan, now)
        current = replace(current, started_at=now - max(0.0, overshoot))
    return current


def reset(state: SessionState) -> SessionState:
    """A fresh session, keeping nothing from the old one."""
    return SessionState.initial()

"""Unit tests for the phase plan, session transitions and the status read model."""

import unittest

from tempo.phases import FOCUS, LONG_BREAK, SHORT_BREAK, PhasePlan
from tempo.session import (SessionState, advanced, elapsed_seconds, paused,
                           remaining_seconds, reset, settled, started)
from tempo.status import snapshot

SHORT_PLAN = PhasePlan(focus_seconds=10, short_break_seconds=5, long_break_seconds=8,
                       cycle_length=2)


class PhasePlanTest(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_sequence_alternates_and_lengthens_every_cycle(self):
        kinds = [SHORT_PLAN.phase_at(index).kind for index in range(6)]
        self.assertEqual([FOCUS, SHORT_BREAK, FOCUS, LONG_BREAK, FOCUS, SHORT_BREAK], kinds)

    def test_negative_index_is_refused(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            SHORT_PLAN.phase_at(-1)

    def test_validated_names_the_bad_field(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "focus_seconds"):
            PhasePlan(focus_seconds=0).validated()
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "cycle_length"):
            PhasePlan(cycle_length=0).validated()
        self.assertEqual(PhasePlan(), PhasePlan().validated())


class SessionTransitionTest(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_pause_banks_elapsed_and_resume_continues(self):
        running = started(SessionState.initial(), 100.0)
        stopped = paused(running, 104.0)
        self.assertFalse(stopped.running)
        self.assertEqual(4.0, stopped.spent_seconds)
        self.assertEqual(4.0, elapsed_seconds(stopped, 999.0))
        self.assertEqual(6.0, remaining_seconds(started(stopped, 200.0), SHORT_PLAN, 200.0))

    def test_repeated_start_and_pause_are_no_ops(self):
        running = started(SessionState.initial(), 10.0)
        self.assertIs(running, started(running, 50.0))
        stopped = paused(running, 12.0)
        self.assertIs(stopped, paused(stopped, 90.0))

    def test_advance_counts_only_finished_focus_phases(self):
        first_break = advanced(SessionState.initial(), SHORT_PLAN, 0.0)
        self.assertEqual(1, first_break.completed_focus)
        self.assertEqual(0, advanced(first_break, SHORT_PLAN, 0.0).completed_focus - 1)

    def test_paused_session_never_settles_forward(self):
        idle = SessionState.initial()
        self.assertIs(idle, settled(idle, SHORT_PLAN, 10_000.0))

    def test_settle_carries_overshoot_into_the_new_phase(self):
        running = started(SessionState.initial(), 0.0)
        landed = settled(running, SHORT_PLAN, 13.0)
        self.assertEqual(1, landed.phase_index)
        self.assertEqual(2.0, elapsed_seconds(landed, 13.0))
        self.assertEqual(1, landed.completed_focus)

    def test_reset_returns_a_fresh_session(self):
        self.assertEqual(SessionState.initial(), reset(settled(started(
            SessionState.initial(), 0.0), SHORT_PLAN, 99.0)))


class SnapshotTest(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_snapshot_reports_whole_seconds_and_cycle_position(self):
        state = settled(started(SessionState.initial(), 0.0), SHORT_PLAN, 12.5)
        payload = snapshot(state, SHORT_PLAN, 12.5)
        self.assertEqual(SHORT_BREAK, payload["phase"])
        self.assertEqual(3, payload["remaining_seconds"])
        self.assertEqual(2, payload["elapsed_seconds"])
        self.assertTrue(payload["running"])
        self.assertEqual(1, payload["completed_focus"])
        self.assertEqual(1, payload["cycle_position"])

    def test_remaining_never_goes_negative(self):
        stuck = SessionState(phase_index=0, running=False, spent_seconds=99.0)
        self.assertEqual(0, snapshot(stuck, SHORT_PLAN, 0.0)["remaining_seconds"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

### PRINCIPLE-018: Automatic Git Workflow (Commit & Push)
- **Problem**: Uncommitted work is lost; blind staging sweeps secrets and clutter into commits; diverged remotes tempt force-pushes; destructive resets erase work. When the rules claim a lock that does not exist, list only some blind-staging forms or give one rollback for every case, each model takes different risks with the user's history.
- **Concept**: The agent commits each verified unit of work with a checked message when git delivery is authorized, stages files by name, pushes without force, and undoes mistakes without discarding anything. The gates are enforced by the agent running them, not by a hook.
- **Invariant**: Conventional commits (`--validate-commit`) + adaptive push, never forced, only if authorized (R1); explicit staging (no `git add .`); pre-commit triad (tests/gates/diff); commit verified alone pre-push (R7); non-destructive recoil.
- **Rules**:
  1. **Automatic Conventional Commits** *[Agent]*: *Commit delivery* is authorized when the user asked in this task for a commit or a pull request, or when the host platform's standing instructions place no explicit-request restriction on git operations the agent starts. *Push delivery* is authorized when the user asked in this task for a push or a pull request, or when the host platform's standing instructions place no explicit-request restriction and the user did not say not to push. Commit delivery is not authorized when the user said not to commit or the host platform forbids commits the user did not explicitly request; push delivery is not authorized when the user said not to push or the host platform forbids pushes the user did not explicitly request. The agent MUST check its host platform's standing instructions before deciding to commit or push, and a restriction there counts as the user not having asked. When commit delivery is authorized and Phase 4 passes for a milestone or a task (PRINCIPLE-006 R1), the agent commits; when it is not authorized, it stops after Phase 4 and reports the uncommitted files. The subject is `type(scope): description` or `type(scope): [milestone N/M] description`, with a type from `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `chore`, `test`, `perf`, `build`, `ci`, and at most 72 characters; `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --validate-commit "<message>"` MUST pass before the commit.
  2. **Explicit Staging Invariant (Zero Blind Staging)** *[Agent]*: The agent stages files only by name (`git add <file> ...`). It MUST NOT run `git add .`, `git add -A`, `git add --all`, `git add -u` or `git commit -a`.
  3. **Pre-Commit Delivery Triad Gate** *[Agent]*: No hook enforces this; except when the informed override of PRINCIPLE-002 R5 applies, the agent MUST NOT commit until all three hold on the tree being committed: (1) both test tiers pass, which `python scripts/check_test_budgets.py` verifies together with their per-test budgets (PRINCIPLE-010 R6); (2) every read-only gate passes: `python scripts/sync_principles.py --check`, `python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py --check`, `python scripts/check_reachability.py`, `python scripts/check_secrets.py` and `python scripts/dogfood.py`; (3) `git status --short` shows exactly the files the change intends staged, and nothing else modified. Items (1) and (2) are Phase 4 (PRINCIPLE-002 R1).
  4. **Adaptive Push & Zero Force Push** *[Agent]*: After a commit the agent pushes to the current branch's upstream when push delivery is authorized (R1); otherwise it reports the commit as local only. A branch without an upstream is pushed with `git push -u origin <branch>` when a remote named `origin` exists; with no remote it reports the commit as local only, and with remotes but none named `origin` it asks the user which to use. When the push is rejected because the remote moved, it runs `git pull --rebase` and pushes again; when the rebase stops on a conflict, it runs `git rebase --abort` and asks the user (PRINCIPLE-003 R6). It MUST NOT run `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease` unless the user asked for that push.
  5. **Non-Destructive Recoil Invariant** *[Agent]*: To undo its own commit that is not yet pushed, the agent runs `git reset --soft HEAD^` (the parent commit); to undo a pushed commit, `git revert <hash>`. It MUST NOT run `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, `git checkout -- <file>`, `git restore <file>` or `git stash drop` on changes it did not make in this task.
  6. **Terse Delivery Confirmation** *[Agent]*: The final message names, for every commit made, its short hash (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), its subject, the number of files and the branch, and says whether it was pushed.
  7. **Post-Commit Verification of the Delivered Commit** *[Agent]*: After each commit, and before R4's push, the agent runs `python scripts/verify_commit.py`; the push follows only when it exits 0. It checks the commit out into a throwaway worktree and runs R3's gates against that commit alone, because R3 proves the working tree is green and the commit is a different tree whenever staging is a subset of it (R2). On a failure the agent undoes the still-unpushed commit with R5's `git reset --soft HEAD^`, adds what the commit lacked, and commits again. A project's commits are verified by `python aikit.py check --strict <name>` instead (PRINCIPLE-011 R8).

---

"""
Crash-safe persistence for one session.

The state file is written to a temporary sibling, flushed, fsynced and moved into place,
so a power loss leaves either the old file or the new one and never a half-written mix.
A file whose schema version this build does not know is refused untouched; a corrupt file
is quarantined and replaced by a fresh session, so the UI always has something to render.

PRINCIPLE-011, PRINCIPLE-013.
"""

import json
import os
import tempfile
from dataclasses import asdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from tempo.session import SessionState

SCHEMA = 1
REPLACE_ATTEMPTS = 5
FIELDS = ("phase_index", "running", "started_at", "spent_seconds", "completed_focus")


class StoreError(RuntimeError):
    """A state file this build must not touch: the caller reports why and the fix."""

    def __init__(self, message: str, why: str, fix: str):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.why = why
        self.fix = fix


def _decode(payload: object) -> SessionState:
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise ValueError("state file is not a JSON object")
    version = payload.get("schema")
    if version != SCHEMA:
        raise StoreError(
            f"session file has schema {version!r}, not {SCHEMA}.",
            "a newer Tempo wrote this session and its fields may mean something else.",
            "upgrade Tempo, or move the file aside to start a fresh session.")
    session = payload.get("session")
    if not isinstance(session, dict) or any(field not in session for field in FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("state file is missing session fields")
    return SessionState(
        phase_index=int(session["phase_index"]),
        running=bool(session["running"]),
        started_at=None if session["started_at"] is None else float(session["started_at"]),
        spent_seconds=float(session["spent_seconds"]),
        completed_focus=int(session["completed_focus"]),
    )


class SessionStore:
    """Reads and writes one session file, atomically and without ever losing the old one."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.quarantine = self.path.with_suffix(self.path.suffix + ".corrupt")

    def load(self) -> SessionState:
        """The stored session, or a fresh one when no readable file exists."""
        if not self.path.exists():
            return SessionState.initial()
        try:
            with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                return _decode(json.load(handle))
        except StoreError:
            raise
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            self._quarantine()
            return SessionState.initial()

    def save(self, state: SessionState) -> None:
        """The session on disk, replaced atomically; the directory is created if missing."""
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        payload = {"schema": SCHEMA, "session": asdict(state)}
        handle = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
            "w", encoding="utf-8", dir=str(self.path.parent),
            prefix=self.path.name + ".", suffix=".tmp", delete=False)
        temporary = Path(handle.name)
        try:
            with handle:
                json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
            self._replace(temporary)
        finally:
            if temporary.exists():
                temporary.unlink()

    def _replace(self, temporary: Path) -> None:
        last: Optional[OSError] = None
        for _ in range(REPLACE_ATTEMPTS):
            try:
                os.replace(str(temporary), str(self.path))
                return
            except OSError as error:
                last = error
        raise StoreError(
            f"could not replace {self.path.name} after {REPLACE_ATTEMPTS} attempts ({last}).",
            "another process is holding the session file open.",
            "close other Tempo servers, then retry.")

    def _quarantine(self) -> None:
        try:
            os.replace(str(self.path), str(self.quarantine))
        except OSError:
            pass

"""Unit tests for atomic session persistence, schema refusal and quarantine."""

import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from tempo.session import SessionState
from tempo.store import SCHEMA, SessionStore, StoreError


class SessionStoreTest(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(directory.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(directory.name)
        self.store = SessionStore(self.root / "state" / "session.json")

    def test_missing_file_reads_as_a_fresh_session(self):
        self.assertEqual(SessionState.initial(), self.store.load())

    def test_round_trip_preserves_every_field(self):
        state = SessionState(phase_index=3, running=True, started_at=12.5,
                             spent_seconds=4.25, completed_focus=2)
        self.store.save(state)
        self.assertEqual(state, self.store.load())

    def test_save_leaves_no_temporary_files_behind(self):
        self.store.save(SessionState.initial())
        leftovers = [path.name for path in self.store.path.parent.iterdir()
                     if path.name != self.store.path.name]
        self.assertEqual([], leftovers)

    def test_unknown_schema_is_refused_without_touching_the_file(self):
        self.store.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.store.path.write_text(json.dumps({"schema": SCHEMA + 1, "session": {}}),
                                   encoding="utf-8")
        before = self.store.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(StoreError) as caught:
            self.store.load()
        self.assertIn("schema", str(caught.exception))
        self.assertEqual(before, self.store.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertFalse(self.store.quarantine.exists())

    def test_corrupt_file_is_quarantined_and_replaced_by_a_fresh_session(self):
        self.store.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.store.path.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(SessionState.initial(), self.store.load())
        self.assertTrue(self.store.quarantine.exists())
        self.assertFalse(self.store.path.exists())

    def test_missing_fields_count_as_corrupt(self):
        self.store.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        self.store.path.write_text(json.dumps({"schema": SCHEMA, "session": {"running": True}}),
                                   encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(SessionState.initial(), self.store.load())
        self.assertTrue(self.store.quarantine.exists())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""
The HTTP layer: a stdlib server that serves web/ and three JSON endpoints.

`TempoApp` is the whole backend contract — settle the stored session against the clock,
apply one named action, hand back the snapshot the UI renders. The request handler only
translates HTTP into those two calls, so the timer can be tested without a socket.

PRINCIPLE-009, PRINCIPLE-010, PRINCIPLE-011, PRINCIPLE-013.
"""

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Dict, Optional, Tuple
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from tempo.phases import PhasePlan
from tempo.session import advanced, paused, reset, settled, started
from tempo.status import snapshot
from tempo.store import SessionStore, StoreError

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 4096
READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10
CONTENT_TYPES = {
    ".html": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
    ".css": "text/css; charset=utf-8",
    ".js": "text/javascript; charset=utf-8",
    ".svg": "image/svg+xml",
}
WEB_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "web"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StaticFiles:
    """Resolves a URL path to a file inside one directory, and never outside it."""

    root: Path

    def resolve(self, url_path: str) -> Optional[Path]:
        """The file a URL path names, or None when it escapes or does not exist."""
        relative = url_path.lstrip("/") or "index.html"
        candidate = (self.root / relative).resolve()
        try:
            candidate.relative_to(self.root.resolve())
        except ValueError:
            return None
        return candidate if candidate.is_file() else None


class TempoApp:
    """One session's backend: settle it against the clock, act on it, report it."""

    ACTIONS = ("toggle", "skip", "reset")

    def __init__(self, store: SessionStore, plan: PhasePlan,
                 clock: Callable[[], float]):
        self.store = store
        self.plan = plan.validated()
        self.clock = clock

    def status(self) -> Dict[str, object]:
        """The current snapshot, persisting any phases that elapsed since the last call."""
        now = self.clock()
        stored = self.store.load()
        current = settled(stored, self.plan, now)
        if current != stored:
            self.store.save(current)
        return snapshot(current, self.plan, now)

    def apply(self, action: str) -> Dict[str, object]:
        """The snapshot after one named action; an unknown action raises ValueError."""
        if action not in self.ACTIONS:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown action {action!r}; expected one of "
                             f"{', '.join(self.ACTIONS)}")
        now = self.clock()
        current = settled(self.store.load(), self.plan, now)
        if action == "toggle":
            current = paused(current, now) if current.running else started(current, now)
        elif action == "skip":
            current = advanced(current, self.plan, now)
        else:
            current = reset(current)
        self.store.save(current)
        return snapshot(current, self.plan, now)


class TempoHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Translates requests into `TempoApp` calls; the app owns every timer rule."""

    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    timeout = READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
    app: Optional[TempoApp] = None
    files: Optional[StaticFiles] = None

    def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - stdlib handler contract
        route = urlparse(self.path).path
        if route == "/api/status":
            self._guarded(lambda: (200, self.app.status()))
            return
        target = self.files.resolve(route)
        if target is None:
            self._json(404, {"error": "not found", "path": route})
            return
        body = target.read_bytes()
        self._respond(200, CONTENT_TYPES.get(target.suffix, "application/octet-stream"),
                      body, cache=route != "/" and not route.endswith(".html"))

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - stdlib handler contract
        if urlparse(self.path).path != "/api/action":
            self._json(404, {"error": "not found", "path": self.path})
            return

from typing import Callable, Dict, Optional, Tuple

READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10

    ".html": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
    ".css": "text/css; charset=utf-8",

class StaticFiles:
    """Resolves a URL path to a file inside one directory, and never outside it."""

    root: Path

    def resolve(self, url_path: str) -> Optional[Path]:
        """The file a URL path names, or None when it escapes or does not exist."""
        relative = url_path.lstrip("/") or "index.html"
        candidate = (self.root / relative).resolve()

"""Integration tests over a real socket: the JSON endpoints and the served page."""

import json
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

from tempo.phases import PhasePlan
from tempo.server import TempoApp, build_server
from tempo.store import SessionStore

WEB = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "web"
TIMEOUT = 5


class HttpTest(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(directory.cleanup)
        self.moment = [500.0]
        app = TempoApp(SessionStore(Path(directory.name) / "session.json"),
                       PhasePlan(focus_seconds=10, short_break_seconds=5, cycle_length=2),
                       lambda: self.moment[0])
        self.server = build_server(app, 0, WEB)
        self.addCleanup(self.server.server_close)
        thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        self.addCleanup(thread.join, TIMEOUT)
        self.addCleanup(self.server.shutdown)
        self.base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"

    def get(self, path):
        with urllib.request.urlopen(self.base + path, timeout=TIMEOUT) as response:
            return response.status, response.headers, response.read()

    def post(self, path, payload):
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            self.base + path, data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=TIMEOUT) as response:
            return response.status, json.loads(response.read())

    def test_status_and_actions_round_trip_over_http(self):
        status, _, body = self.get("/api/status")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual(10, json.loads(body)["remaining_seconds"])
        _, started = self.post("/api/action", {"action": "toggle"})
        self.assertTrue(started["running"])
        self.moment[0] += 3
        _, _, polled = self.get("/api/status")
        self.assertEqual(7, json.loads(polled)["remaining_seconds"])

    def test_the_page_and_its_assets_are_served_with_their_types(self):
        for path, expected in (("/", "text/html"), ("/app.js", "text/javascript"),
                               ("/theme.css", "text/css")):
            status, headers, body = self.get(path)
            self.assertEqual(200, status)
            self.assertIn(expected, headers["Content-Type"])
            self.assertTrue(body)

    def test_an_unknown_action_answers_400_with_a_reason(self):
        with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as caught:
            self.post("/api/action", {"action": "explode"})
        self.assertEqual(400, caught.exception.code)
        self.assertIn("unknown action", json.loads(caught.exception.read())["error"])

    def test_unknown_paths_answer_404(self):
        for method in ("GET", "POST"):
            request = urllib.request.Request(self.base + "/nope", method=method,
                                             data=b"{}" if method == "POST" else None)
            with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as caught:
                urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=TIMEOUT)
            self.assertEqual(404, caught.exception.code)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

        self.addCleanup(self.server.server_close)
        thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)

        self.addCleanup(self.server.shutdown)
        self.base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"

    def get(self, path):
        with urllib.request.urlopen(self.base + path, timeout=TIMEOUT) as response:
            return response.status, response.headers, response.read()

    def post(self, path, payload):
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            self.base + path, data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=TIMEOUT) as response:
            return response.status, json.loads(response.read())

        self.assertEqual(200, status)

        _, started = self.post("/api/action", {"action": "toggle"})
        self.assertTrue(started["running"])

        _, _, polled = self.get("/api/status")
        self.assertEqual(7, json.loads(polled)["remaining_seconds"])

    def test_the_page_and_its_assets_are_served_with_their_types(self):
        for path, expected in (("/", "text/html"), ("/app.js", "text/javascript"),
                               ("/theme.css", "text/css")):
            status, headers, body = self.get(path)
            self.assertEqual(200, status)
            self.assertIn(expected, headers["Content-Type"])
            self.assertTrue(body)

        with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as caught:
            self.post("/api/action", {"action": "explode"})
        self.assertEqual(400, caught.exception.code)
        self.assertIn("unknown action", json.loads(caught.exception.read())["error"])

    def test_unknown_paths_answer_404(self):
        for method in ("GET", "POST"):
            request = urllib.request.Request(self.base + "/nope", method=method,
                                             data=b"{}" if method == "POST" else None)
            with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as caught:
                urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=TIMEOUT)
            self.assertEqual(404, caught.exception.code)

cat > README.md <<'MD'
# tempo

A focus timer you run on your own machine: one Python process, a browser page, no
dependencies, no account and no network calls. Phases alternate focus and break, and
every fourth break is a long one.

## ⚡ 30-Second Cold-Start Quick Reference

- **Runtime Prerequisites**: Python 3.9+ (standard library only — nothing to install) and
  any modern browser.
- **Start it**:
  ```bash
  python run.py            # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765
  ```
- **Canonical Regression Shield Gate**:
  ```bash
  python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
  ```
- **UI inventory proof** (the snapshot the UI guard compares against):
  ```bash
  python tools/ui_inventory.py
  ```

### 🛠️ AIKit Commands (run from the AIKit folder)
| Role | Command |
|---|---|
| Status, task and gates | `python aikit.py status tempo` |
| Phase 4: every gate | `python aikit.py check tempo` |
| Repair memory and map, then check | `python aikit.py fix tempo` |
| Resume an interrupted task | `python aikit.py resume tempo` |
| Open a bounded UI task | `python aikit.py ui begin tempo "<what>"` |
| Check scope, proofs and style | `python aikit.py ui verify tempo` |

## 📦 What's Inside

```text
tempo/
├── run.py                    <- entry point: flags, port, phase lengths
├── tempo/
│   ├── phases.py             <- the phase sequence and its durations (pure)
│   ├── session.py            <- session state and its transitions (pure)
│   ├── status.py             <- the flat read model the UI renders
│   ├── store.py              <- atomic, power-loss-safe session file
│   └── server.py             <- stdlib HTTP: web/ plus two JSON endpoints
├── web/
│   ├── index.html            <- the page: controls, live regions, roles
│   ├── theme.css             <- every colour, font and token (the only theme path)
│   ├── app.css               <- layout only: box model, flow, spacing
│   └── app.js                <- polls status, posts one named action per button
├── tools/
│   └── ui_inventory.py       <- prints the UI inventory, one entry per line
├── tests/
│   ├── test_session.py       <- phase plan, transitions, read model
│   ├── test_store.py         <- round trip, schema refusal, quarantine
│   ├── test_app.py           <- backend contract and static path safety
│   └── test_http.py          <- real socket: endpoints, assets, 400s and 404s
├── README.md
└── .aikit/                   <- this project's memory: record, ledger, decisions
```

## 🎛️ Using it

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Start / Pause** | Runs or banks the current phase. Space does the same. |
| **Skip phase** | Moves to the next phase; a skipped focus phase still counts. |
| **Reset** | Back to a paused first focus phase, cycle count cleared. |

Flags: `--port`, `--state`, `--focus`, `--short-break`, `--long-break`, `--cycle`
(minutes, except `--cycle`, which counts focus phases before a long break). Bad values
exit 2 with a `Why:` and a `Fix:`; a taken port exits 1.

## 🧭 How it is put together

The timer owns no clock. `session.py` takes `now` as an argument and returns new frozen
states, so every rule is testable without sleeping. `settled()` advances past phases that
elapsed between two polls and carries the overshoot forward, which is why the browser can
poll once a second — or once a minute — and still land on the right phase.

The server settles, persists and reports; the page only renders what it is given. All
colour and type live in `web/theme.css`, so a hardcoded colour anywhere else in `web/` is
a style-drift finding rather than a matter of taste.

### State and crashes

`state/session.json` is written to a temporary sibling, flushed, fsynced and moved into
place, so a power loss leaves the old file or the new one, never half of each. The file
carries a schema version: a version this build does not know is refused untouched, and an
unreadable file is moved to `session.json.corrupt` and replaced by a fresh session.
MD

# tempo

A focus timer you run on your own machine: one Python process, a browser page, no
dependencies, no account and no network calls. Phases alternate focus and break, and
every fourth break is a long one.

## ⚡ 30-Second Cold-Start Quick Reference

- **Runtime Prerequisites**: Python 3.9+ (standard library only — nothing to install) and
  any modern browser.
- **Start it**:
  ```bash
  python run.py            # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765
  ```
- **Canonical Regression Shield Gate**:
  ```bash
  python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
  ```
- **UI inventory proof** (the snapshot the UI guard compares against):
  ```bash
  python tools/ui_inventory.py
  ```

### 🛠️ AIKit Commands (run from the AIKit folder)
| Role | Command |
|---|---|
| Status, task and gates | `python aikit.py status tempo` |
| Phase 4: every gate | `python aikit.py check tempo` |
| Repair memory and map, then check | `python aikit.py fix tempo` |
| Resume an interrupted task | `python aikit.py resume tempo` |
| Open a bounded UI task | `python aikit.py ui begin tempo "<what>"` |
| Check scope, proofs and style | `python aikit.py ui verify tempo` |

## 📦 What's Inside

```text
tempo/
├── run.py                    <- entry point: flags, port, phase lengths
├── tempo/
│   ├── phases.py             <- the phase sequence and its durations (pure)
│   ├── session.py            <- session state and its transitions (pure)
│   ├── status.py             <- the flat read model the UI renders
│   ├── store.py              <- atomic, power-loss-safe session file
│   └── server.py             <- stdlib HTTP: web/ plus two JSON endpoints
├── web/
│   ├── index.html            <- the page: controls, live regions, roles
│   ├── theme.css             <- every colour, font and token (the only theme path)
│   ├── app.css               <- layout only: box model, flow, spacing
│   └── app.js                <- polls status, posts one named action per button
├── tools/
│   └── ui_inventory.py       <- prints the UI inventory, one entry per line
├── tests/
│   ├── test_session.py       <- phase plan, transitions, read model
│   ├── test_store.py         <- round trip, schema refusal, quarantine
│   ├── test_app.py           <- backend contract and static path safety
│   └── test_http.py          <- real socket: endpoints, assets, 400s and 404s
├── README.md
└── .aikit/                   <- this project's memory: record, ledger, decisions
```

## 🎛️ Using it

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Start / Pause** | Runs or banks the current phase. Space does the same. |
| **Skip phase** | Moves to the next phase; a skipped focus phase still counts. |
| **Reset** | Back to a paused first focus phase, cycle count cleared. |

Flags: `--port`, `--state`, `--focus`, `--short-break`, `--long-break`, `--cycle`
(minutes, except `--cycle`, which counts focus phases before a long break). Bad values
exit 2 with a `Why:` and a `Fix:`; a taken port exits 1.

## 🧭 How it is put together

The timer owns no clock. `session.py` takes `now` as an argument and returns new frozen
states, so every rule is testable without sleeping. `settled()` advances past phases that
elapsed between two polls and carries the overshoot forward, which is why the browser can
poll once a second — or once a minute — and still land on the right phase.

The server settles, persists and reports; the page only renders what it is given. All
colour and type live in `web/theme.css`, so a hardcoded colour anywhere else in `web/` is
a style-drift finding rather than a matter of taste.

### State and crashes

`state/session.json` is written to a temporary sibling, flushed, fsynced and moved into
place, so a power loss leaves the old file or the new one, never half of each. The file
carries a schema version: a version this build does not know is refused untouched, and an
unreadable file is moved to `session.json.corrupt` and replaced by a fresh session.

### PRINCIPLE-015: Universal Operational Dogfooding & Chaos Verification (The AI Must Use What It Builds)
- **Problem**: Unit tests in isolation miss real interaction bugs; dev servers leak zombie processes; prompts hang in subshells; a page can return HTTP 200 and render nothing; GUI windows crash without a display. When the rules do not say whose runner they mean, when it runs, or which of three line limits applies, each model dogfoods differently or not at all.
- **Concept**: The agent runs what it builds the way a user would, in a sandbox, on the golden path and under one hostile input, and the run is a commit gate. AIKit's `scripts/dogfood.py` does this for AIKit's own tools; a project built with AIKit has its own runner for its own product.
- **Invariant**: Domain-specific interactive dogfooding via `scripts/dogfood.py` as a commit gate; golden path + chaos perturbation; non-interactive stdin parity; portable RAII process tree teardown; ephemeral safety jail; terse reporting (<=15 lines).
- **Rules**:
  1. **Domain-Specific Interactive Dogfooding & Headless Parity** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: The project's dogfood runner exercises its product the way its users do, by product type. A desktop GUI is opened (offscreen or a virtual display), its controls are used and its window destroyed within 10 seconds, with no unhandled callback exception. A web app is served on a free port, loaded in a headless browser, and its root container (`#root`, `#app`) has rendered children and no `console.error`. A CLI runs as a real process with real arguments and closed stdin, and its exit codes are checked. A backend API is started, called over HTTP, and answers with the declared status, schema, and within 500ms. AIKit's runner is `python scripts/dogfood.py`, for AIKit's CLIs; an adopting project writes its own.
  2. **Platform-Portable Process Tree Teardown (RAII Cleanup)** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: Every process a runner starts runs inside a context manager that, on exit or on a failed assertion, kills the whole process tree: `taskkill /F /T /PID <pid>` on Windows, `os.killpg(pid, signal.SIGKILL)` on POSIX. AIKit's is `supervised` with `terminate_process_tree`.
  3. **Non-Interactive Stdin Parity & EOF Safety** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: The runner starts every command with stdin closed, so a command that waits for input fails the run; the duty itself is PRINCIPLE-011 R2 and R5.
  4. **Hermetic Ephemeral State & Storage Sandboxing** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: Everything a run writes (state files, databases, caches) goes under one temporary sandbox directory created for the run; the one exception is R7's run log, which MUST be listed in `.gitignore`. The runner records a content fingerprint of the repository's tracked files before and after the run and fails when it changed; it MUST NOT write to the user's home folders.
  5. **Dual-Track Dogfooding (Golden Path + Hostile Chaos Perturbation)** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: Every run executes (1) one end-to-end golden path that creates, changes and reads back the product's main object, and (2) at least one hostile input (an interrupt, an invalid value, malformed JSON or concurrent requests). Running `--help` alone is not a dogfood run.
  6. **Deterministic Domain Exit Contracts** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: A run passes only when every step met its R1 criterion and no traceback appeared on stderr.
  7. **Terse Context Reporting & Pre-Ship Gate** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: The runner prints at most 15 lines and writes everything else to a log file (`.agents/dogfood_last_run.log` in AIKit). It is one of PRINCIPLE-018 R3's commit gates and runs in Phase 4 (PRINCIPLE-002 R1).
  8. **Realistic Live Budgeting & Sanity Guardrails** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: A dogfood run that calls a live paid provider obeys the step and token caps of PRINCIPLE-012 R6.

---

## 🚀 Phase 5: Living Synchronization & Delivery

### PRINCIPLE-016: AI Knowledge Base & Continuous Synchronization

"""
Tempo's own dogfood runner: use the product the way a user does, then attack it.

The golden path starts a real server on a free port, loads the page, drives the controls
over HTTP and reads the session back. The chaos track then feeds it malformed JSON, an

import contextlib
import hashlib
import json
import os
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import urllib.error

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

LOG_PATH = ROOT / ".aikit" / "dogfood_last_run.log"
MAX_REPORT_LINES = 15
START_TIMEOUT = 20.0
REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 5.0
API_BUDGET_MS = 500.0

                 "cycle_length")


class Report:
    """Collects step outcomes: the console sees a summary, the log sees everything."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.lines: List[str] = []
        self.failures: List[str] = []

    def step(self, ok: bool, label: str, detail: str = "") -> bool:
        mark = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
        self.lines.append(f"[{mark}] {label}" + (f" :: {detail}" if detail else ""))
        if not ok:
            self.failures.append(f"{label}: {detail}" if detail else label)
        return ok


def terminate_process_tree(process: subprocess.Popen) -> None:
    """Kill a process and everything it started, on Windows and on POSIX alike."""
    if process.poll() is not None:
        return
    try:
        if os.name == "nt":
            subprocess.run(["taskkill", "/F", "/T", "/PID", str(process.pid)],
                           capture_output=True, timeout=GIT_TIMEOUT)
        else:
            os.killpg(os.getpgid(process.pid), signal.SIGKILL)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        process.kill()
    with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        process.wait(timeout=10)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def supervised(command: List[str], log) -> subprocess.Popen:
    """Run a command with stdin closed (R3), killing its whole tree on the way out (R2)."""
    creation = {"creationflags": subprocess.CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP} if os.name == "nt" \
        else {"start_new_session": True}
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=log,
                               stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, cwd=str(ROOT), **creation)
    try:
        yield process
    finally:
        terminate_process_tree(process)


def free_port() -> int:
    """A port the operating system says is free right now."""
    with socket.socket() as probe:

    listing = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "-z"], cwd=str(ROOT), capture_output=True,
                             timeout=GIT_TIMEOUT)
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in sorted(part for part in listing.stdout.split(b"\0") if part):
        digest.update(name)

    report.step(code == 200 and all(field in payload for field in STATUS_FIELDS),
                "GET /api/status answers the declared schema", f"HTTP {code}")
    report.step(elapsed < API_BUDGET_MS, "status answers inside its 500ms budget",
                f"{elapsed:.0f}ms")

    code, body = post(base, {"action": "toggle"})
    report.step(code == 200 and json.loads(body)["running"] is True, "toggle starts the timer")

    done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "ui_inventory.py")],
                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=GIT_TIMEOUT, cwd=str(ROOT))

    report.step(done.returncode == 0 and len(entries) >= 20,

    with urllib.request.urlopen(base + path, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT) as response:
        body = response.read()
        status = response.status
    return status, body, (time.monotonic() - started) * 1000.0


def post(base: str, payload: object, raw: Optional[bytes] = None) -> Tuple[int, bytes]:
    """One action POST; an HTTP error is an answer here, not an exception."""
    data = raw if raw is not None else json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
    request = urllib.request.Request(base + "/api/action", data=data, method="POST",
                                     headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT) as response:
            return response.status, response.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        with error:
            return error.code, error.read()


def wait_until_serving(base: str) -> bool:
    """True once the server answers, False if it never does within the start timeout."""
    deadline = time.monotonic() + START_TIMEOUT
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        try:
            get(base, "/api/status")
            return True
        except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError):
            time.sleep(0.05)
    return False


def golden_path(base: str, state: Path, report: Report) -> None:
    """Load the page, run the timer through a phase change, read the session back (R5)."""
    status, page, _ = get(base, "/")
    report.step(status == 200 and all(control in page for control in CONTROLS),
                "page serves every control the script renders into",
                f"HTTP {status}, {len(page)} bytes")

    code, body, elapsed = get(base, "/api/status")
    first = json.loads(body)
    report.step(code == 200 and all(field in first for field in STATUS_FIELDS),
                "GET /api/status answers the declared schema", f"HTTP {code}")
    report.step(elapsed < API_BUDGET_MS, "status answers inside its 500ms budget",
                f"{elapsed:.0f}ms")

    code, body = post(base, {"action": "toggle"})
    report.step(code == 200 and json.loads(body)["running"] is True,
                "toggle starts the timer", f"HTTP {code}")

    time.sleep(1.1)
    counted = json.loads(get(base, "/api/status")[1])
    report.step(counted["remaining_seconds"] < first["remaining_seconds"],
                "the clock advances while running",
                f"{first['remaining_seconds']}s -> {counted['remaining_seconds']}s")

    time.sleep(2.2)
    rolled = json.loads(get(base, "/api/status")[1])
    report.step(rolled["phase"] == "short-break" and rolled["completed_focus"] == 1,
                "a finished focus phase rolls into the break and is counted",
                f"{rolled['phase']}, {rolled['completed_focus']} done")
    report.step(state.is_file()
                and json.loads(state.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["schema"] == 1,
                "the session is persisted with its schema version")

    code, body = post(base, {"action": "reset"})
    report.step(code == 200 and json.loads(body)["completed_focus"] == 0,
                "reset clears the session", f"HTTP {code}")


def chaos(base: str, state: Path, report: Report) -> None:
    """Hostile inputs: malformed JSON, bad values, a flood and a corrupt session (R5)."""
    code, body = post(base, None, raw=b"{not json at all")
    report.step(code == 400 and b"error" in body, "malformed JSON answers 400", f"HTTP {code}")

    code, body = post(base, {"action": "self-destruct"})
    report.step(code == 400 and b"unknown action" in body, "unknown action answers 400",
                f"HTTP {code}")

    padded = b'{"action":"toggle","pad":"' + b"x" * 8192 + b'"}'
    code, _ = post(base, None, raw=padded)
    report.step(code == 413, "an oversized body answers 413", f"HTTP {code}")

    code, _ = post(base, [1, 2, 3])
    report.step(code == 400, "a JSON array body answers 400", f"HTTP {code}")

    results: Dict[int, int] = {}
    lock = threading.Lock()

    def hammer() -> None:
        try:
            status = get(base, "/api/status")[0]
        except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError):
            status = 0
        with lock:
            results[status] = results.get(status, 0) + 1

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=hammer) for _ in range(12)]
    for thread in threads:
        thread.start()
    for thread in threads:
        thread.join(REQUEST_TIMEOUT * 2)
    report.step(results.get(200) == len(threads), "12 concurrent polls all answer 200",
                str(results))

    state.write_text("{ truncated", encoding="utf-8")
    code, body, _ = get(base, "/api/status")
    report.step(code == 200 and json.loads(body)["phase"] == "focus",
                "a corrupt session file is quarantined and the UI still renders",
                f"HTTP {code}")
    report.step(state.with_suffix(state.suffix + ".corrupt").is_file(),
                "the unreadable session is kept for inspection")


def surface_proof(report: Report, log) -> None:
    """The UI inventory proof runs and reports its surface, as the UI guard expects."""
    done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "tools" / "ui_inventory.py")],
                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT,
                          cwd=str(ROOT))
    log.write(done.stdout + done.stderr)
    entries = [line for line in done.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    report.step(done.returncode == 0 and len(entries) >= 20,
                "the UI inventory proof reports its surface", f"{len(entries)} entries")


def main() -> int:
    """Run both tracks in one sandbox and print at most 15 lines (R6, R7)."""
    LOG_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report = Report()
    before = fingerprint()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="tempo-dogfood-") as box:
        with open(LOG_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as log:
            state = Path(box) / "session.json"
            port = free_port()
            base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
            command = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "run.py"), "--port", str(port),
                       "--state", str(state), "--focus", "0.05"]
            alive = False
            with supervised(command, log) as process:
                if wait_until_serving(base):
                    report.step(True, "the server starts and answers", base)
                    golden_path(base, state, report)
                    chaos(base, state, report)
                else:
                    report.step(False, "the server starts and answers",
                                f"no answer within {START_TIMEOUT:.0f}s")
                alive = process.poll() is None
            report.step(alive, "the server survived every hostile input")
            surface_proof(report, log)
            log.write("\n".join(report.lines) + "\n")

    report.step(fingerprint() == before, "the run left the tracked tree untouched")
    passed = len(report.lines) - len(report.failures)
    print(f"TEMPO DOGFOOD (PRINCIPLE-015): {passed}/{len(report.lines)} steps passed")
    for failure in report.failures[:MAX_REPORT_LINES - 4]:
        print(f"  [FAIL] {failure}")
    print(f"  full log: {LOG_PATH.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()}")
    if report.failures:
        print("Why: the product must work and hold up under hostile input before it ships.")
        print("Fix: read the log, fix the failing step, then rerun this command.")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

cat >> .aikit/decisions.md <<'MD'

### ADR-001: The timer owns no clock; `now` is always an argument
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: A focus timer tested by sleeping is slow and flaky, and a browser cannot be relied on to poll every second.
- **Decision**: `tempo/session.py` holds frozen states and pure transitions that take `now`. `settled()` advances past phases that elapsed between two polls and carries the overshoot into the new phase.
- **Consequences**: Every timer rule is unit-testable without sleeping, and a page that polls late lands on the same phase it would have reached by polling every second. The cost is that callers must thread a clock through; `TempoApp` holds the only one.

### ADR-002: All colour and type live in `web/theme.css`, the contract's single theme path
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: AIKit's style-drift lint only reports literals outside the theme paths a UI contract declares; with no theme path declared, the lint is off entirely.
- **Decision**: `web/theme.css` holds every colour, font and token, including the dark-mode block. `web/app.css` carries layout only, and `web/app.js` sets a `data-phase` attribute rather than any style. `.aikit/ui.json` declares `theme_paths: ["web/theme.css"]`.
- **Consequences**: A hardcoded colour or font anywhere else in `web/` is a mechanical finding rather than a matter of taste. The cost is that typography declarations cannot be written next to the layout they affect, which is why `.readout` is split across the two files.

### ADR-003: The snapshot proof is a parsed inventory, not a rendered screenshot
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: PRINCIPLE-015 R1 asks a web app to be loaded in a headless browser, but Tempo declares no dependencies and the standard library ships no browser engine.
- **Decision**: `tools/ui_inventory.py` parses `web/` and prints one line per identified element, named action, ARIA role, live region, script handler and theme token. `tools/dogfood.py` satisfies the backend-API criterion in full over a real socket and checks that the served page carries every control the script renders into.
- **Consequences**: A dropped control, action, role, live region or theme token is caught as a lost inventory line, and accessibility attributes are guarded alongside controls. A purely visual regression that keeps the inventory intact is not caught; that gap is deliberate and is the price of zero dependencies.
MD

### ADR-001: The timer owns no clock; `now` is always an argument
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: A focus timer tested by sleeping is slow and flaky, and a browser cannot be relied on to poll every second.
- **Decision**: `tempo/session.py` holds frozen states and pure transitions that take `now`. `settled()` advances past phases that elapsed between two polls and carries the overshoot into the new phase.
- **Consequences**: Every timer rule is unit-testable without sleeping, and a page that polls late lands on the same phase it would have reached by polling every second. The cost is that callers must thread a clock through; `TempoApp` holds the only one.

### ADR-002: All colour and type live in `web/theme.css`, the contract's single theme path
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: AIKit's style-drift lint only reports literals outside the theme paths a UI contract declares; with no theme path declared, the lint is off entirely.
- **Decision**: `web/theme.css` holds every colour, font and token, including the dark-mode block. `web/app.css` carries layout only, and `web/app.js` sets a `data-phase` attribute rather than any style. `.aikit/ui.json` declares `theme_paths: ["web/theme.css"]`.
- **Consequences**: A hardcoded colour or font anywhere else in `web/` is a mechanical finding rather than a matter of taste. The cost is that typography declarations cannot be written next to the layout they affect, which is why `.readout` is split across the two files.

- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
